For positive score rᵢ and K negative occurrences, paper Eq. 16 defines sⱼ = exp(rⱼ)/Σₖexp(rₖ) and L = −log[Σⱼsⱼσ(rᵢ−rⱼ)] + λΣⱼsⱼrⱼ². This is a log of a weighted sigmoid sum, not a weighted sum of BPR losses. Regularization penalizes negative output scores, weighted toward high scores; it is separate from parameter weight decay. Algebraically, with exactly one negative, s₁=1 and L=softplus(r₁−rᵢ)+λr₁²: ordinary pairwise BPR plus negative-score regularization, with no hard-negative weighting effect. [Paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf)

Official sampling uses B−1 other minibatch targets plus n_sample additional draws shared across rows: K=B−1+n_sample negative slots, not necessarily unique items. Additional draws are independent, with replacement, from q(item)∝training-frequency(item)^sample_alpha; α=0 is uniform, α=1 popularity sampling. Minibatch negatives are implicitly popularity-biased. n_sample=2048 is a common setting, not an objective requirement. [Original implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/blob/master/gru4rec.py)

The official code masks only each row’s designated positive diagonal slot before normalizing negative weights. It does not deduplicate candidates, reject other occurrences matching that positive, or exclude historical positives; duplicates retain multiplicity and accidental positives remain negative slots. Both loss terms backpropagate through the softmax weights: do not detach them. The implementation adds 1e−24 inside log, sums row losses, then divides by configured batch size. Official PyTorch optionally applies ELU to scores before both weighting and loss; its logQ correction applies only to cross-entropy. Filtering accidental positives would therefore be an explicit deviation from this implementation. [Official PyTorch code](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/blob/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py)
